newsitem.title: INDIA: India rubber prices dip on low auto sector demand.
newsitem.headline: India rubber prices dip on low auto sector demand.

text.p: Indian rubber prices have fallen to a three-year low due to lack of demand from the automobile sector, planters and traders said on Thursday.
They said Indian rubber was currently 44 rupees per kg compared with 46 rupees in January and 56 rupees in the same period last year.
Indian rubber prices normally rise between February and July, considered the lean months of the season.
"Usually when the lean season starts, prices tend to look up as the demand strengthens against supply," said George Thomas, a leading dealer.
"But this year, there is a general slackening in the consumer sector, particularly automobiles, and therefore prices remain low."
Buta Singh, another dealer, said: "The truck tyre sector accounts for 70 percent of the tyre demand but we are facing a shortfall in demand of about 50,000 tyres per month."
The state-run Rubber Board has estimated the country's rubber output in January at around 59,000 tonnes against a demand of 50,000 tonnes.
Traders said production had outstripped consumption from September 1996 to January. But from February, consumption was expected to outstrip production.
The board has estimated rubber production in 1996/97 (April-March) at 549,000 tonnes against 506,910 tonnes last year.
